Karwa Chauth Bank Holiday: Shimla Branches Face Closure While Rest of India Remains Open

Regional RBI Holiday Schedule Explained

Bank customers across India should verify local branch schedules before planning in-person visits as festive closures take effect. According to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) official holiday calendar, Karwa Chauth brings a location-specific bank closure to Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, on October 29. Public and private sector institutions—including State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, and Bank of Baroda—will keep their Shimla branches shut for the day.

However, this observance does not apply nationwide. Bank branches in all other cities across the country will remain open for regular business on Karwa Chauth, operating under standard working hours.

Upcoming End-of-October and Early-November Closures

Following the mid-week observance in Shimla, the holiday calendar includes additional regional and weekly closures. Bank branches in Ahmedabad are scheduled to close on Saturday, October 31, to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Shortly after, on Sunday, November 1, financial institutions nationwide will observe their standard weekly Sunday holiday.

Account holders with pending paperwork, physical document submissions, or other branch-dependent requirements are advised to factor these specific dates into their schedules to avoid delays.

Digital Banking Availability

While physical branches may be closed in specific locations, digital and automated banking channels remain operational. Customers can continue using Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for transfers, internet and mobile banking platforms for NEFT and RTGS transactions, and debit or credit cards for payments. Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) will also remain functional for cash withdrawals.

Services requiring physical documentation, direct teller assistance, or safe deposit locker access will remain unavailable until the respective branches reopen following the holiday.

Practical Implications and Verification

Bank holidays in India are determined by a combination of national, regional, and state-specific observances listed on the RBI calendar, meaning closures in one municipality do not automatically translate to nationwide shutdowns.

Readers can verify official holiday schedules and confirm local branch statuses directly through the Reserve Bank of India's official portal at https://news.abplive.com/business/personal-finance/karwa-chauth-bank-holiday-are-banks-open-or-closed-october-29-1873579.
